# Heliox OS

> Heliox OS is an MIT-licensed, local-first desktop agent for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It turns natural-language, voice, gesture, browser, and system requests into validated action plans with permission gates and post-execution verification.

Current public release: 0.10.1. Heliox OS is an application-layer desktop agent, not an operating-system kernel, medical device, or proven live brain-control system. Local Ollama models are supported; users may instead configure external model providers, in which case task context is sent directly to the selected provider under that provider's terms. Hardware-dependent features require testing on the user's device. Learned systems may add caution or ranking but cannot grant authority or remove deterministic safety warnings.

- [Machine-readable capability catalog](https://www.helioxos.dev/capabilities.json): Generated action types, platform declarations, permission and approval requirements, specialist providers, verifier coverage, and plugin manifests.

- [Releases](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS/releases): Official installers and release notes.
- [Generated changelog](https://www.helioxos.dev/changelog.md): Versioned product milestones generated from the daemon's shipped changelog.
- [Machine-readable releases](https://www.helioxos.dev/releases.json): Current version and structured feature records.
- [JSON Feed](https://www.helioxos.dev/releases.feed.json): JSON Feed 1.1 release updates.
- [RSS Feed](https://www.helioxos.dev/releases.xml): RSS 2.0 release updates.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS): MIT-licensed source and project documentation.

## Trust and Safety

- [Evidence and limitations](https://www.helioxos.dev/proof.md): Generated capability coverage, live CI links, measured local latency, hardware claim boundaries, known limitations, and representative closed regressions.
- [Privacy policy](https://www.helioxos.dev/privacy.html.md): Local records, external providers, credentials, sensors, and telemetry boundaries.
- [Security overview](https://www.helioxos.dev/whitepaper.html.md): Permission tiers, source-scoped authority, auditing, rollback, and known limits.
- [Detailed security policy](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Current implementation-specific threat model and vulnerability reporting.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/VyomKulshrestha/Heliox-OS/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): Runtime components, data flows, and authority boundaries.

## Use Cases

- [Voice-controlled desktop automation](https://www.helioxos.dev/voice-control.md): Voice input, continuous listening, approvals, spoken status, and hardware limits.
- [Browser and application control](https://www.helioxos.dev/browser-app-control.md): Target resolution, supported actions, verification, and failure boundaries.
- [Accessibility and hands-free operation](https://www.helioxos.dev/accessibility-hands-free.md): Multiple input modes, stop paths, and the non-certified research boundary.
- [Gesture and gaze control](https://www.helioxos.dev/gesture-gaze-control.md): On-device visual signals, temporal confirmation, calibration, and physical-camera limits.
- [Autonomous workflows](https://www.helioxos.dev/autonomous-workflows.md): Durable jobs, bounded parallelism, interruptions, and supervision.
- [Plugin marketplace](https://www.helioxos.dev/plugin-marketplace.md): Moderated submissions, file-integrity checks, capability declarations, and runtime limits.
- [Recorded-EEG and neural research](https://www.helioxos.dev/neural-research.md): Synthetic and recorded-data validation without a live brain-control claim.

## Comparisons

- [Heliox OS vs Copilot on Windows](https://www.helioxos.dev/heliox-vs-windows-copilot.md): Execution scope, platform, permissions, privacy path, and practical fit using Microsoft sources.
- [Heliox OS vs Open Interpreter](https://www.helioxos.dev/heliox-vs-open-interpreter.md): Current agent focus, execution model, extensibility, interfaces, license, and practical fit using the current official repository.
- [Heliox OS vs traditional automation](https://www.helioxos.dev/heliox-vs-traditional-automation.md): Language planning versus scripts, macros, and RPA, including where deterministic automation is better.
